newsitem.title: HONG KONG: A third of HK factories break export rules - customs.
newsitem.headline: A third of HK factories break export rules - customs.

text.p: Almost one in three textile factories in Hong Kong visited during a recent joint U.S.-Hong Kong customs inspection could face prosecution for illegal exports, a senior Hong Kong customs official said on Wednesday.
John Chan, head of Hong Kong Customs' trade controls unit, said authorities had "adequate evidence" to act against 17 of 56 factories inspected during the January visits.
"We visited 56 factories and found 17 to have broken the rules," Chan told Reuters.
"We have adequate evidence of these 17 factories involved in illegal transshipment," he said. "But we are still looking into the matter before we take any action."
Washington imposed tough import measures against Hong Kong's garment exporters last June in a bid to stem illegal transshipments from China via Hong Kong to the United States.
Washington says manufacturers in China dodge quota limits by attaching false "Made in Hong Kong" labels.

U.S. customs had since been allowed to join Hong Kong customs officials on visits to the territory's textile factories as part of the local government's effort to underline its efforts to detect and prevent illegal transshipments.

Since the crackdown, the United States has announced it will lift a single-entry bond imposed on Hong Kong exporters in eight of 10 categories of garments from May 1 and four other categories of textile products will be removed from a watchlist.
